material.text: The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. It is named after the engineer Gustave Eiffel, whose company designed and built the tower from 1887 to 1889. Locally nicknamed La dame de fer, it was constructed as the centerpiece of the 1889 World's Fair. The tower is 330 metres tall, about the same height as an 81-storey building. It was the tallest human-made structure in the world until the Chrysler Building in New York City was finished in 1930.

Eiffel Tower, Parisian landmark and one of the most recognizable structures in the world. It was built for the Exposition Universelle of 1889. Its height including antennas is 330 metres, or 1,083 feet. Maurice Koechlin and Emile Nouguier, two senior engineers working for Gustave Eiffel, made the initial design. More than seven million people visit the tower every year, which makes it one of the most visited paid monuments on Earth.

answer: The tower is 330 metres tall, about the same height as an 81-storey building. It was built for the Exposition Universelle of 1889.
